level.title: Arabic A1+ — Getting around
goals: Ask for directions, tickets and things you need
Give a phone number, an address and a price
Name the days, tell the time and make a plan — or refuse one politely

lessons.title: Right, left, straight: polite directions
lessons.learn: Directions are imperatives, and in Arabic the polite imperative is the point: انعطف يميناً is an order, انعطف يميناً من فضلك is a request. Learn four you will use every day: يمين، شمال، مستقيم، إلى الأمام.

grammar.title: Polite imperative
grammar.explain: انعطف يميناً، ثمّ سِرْ مستقيماً. Add من فضلك and it becomes a request you can make of a stranger. To a woman: انعطفي، سيري.

examples.t: سِرْ مستقيماً ثمّ اسأل مرة أخرى.
examples.r: sir mustaqīman thumma isʾal marra ukhrā.

mistakes.why: يمين takes the accusative -an as an adverb here.
مستقيماً is already an adverbial accusative; في is not needed.

dialogue.en: Please, where is the train station?

dialogue.t: سِرْ مستقيماً ثمّ انعطف يميناً عند المسجد.
dialogue.r: sir mustaqīman thumma inʿaṭif yamīnan ʿinda al-masjid.
dialogue.en: Go straight, then turn right at the mosque.
And is it far from here?

dialogue.t: خمس دقائق على القدمين، ليست بعيدة.
dialogue.r: khams daqāʾiq ʿalā al-qadamayn, laysat baʿīda.
dialogue.en: Five minutes on foot — it is not far.

lessons.title: Tickets, fare and the driver
lessons.learn: A ticket is a transaction, and Arabic transactions are short: أريد تذكرة إلى…، بكم؟، متى يتحرّك القطار؟ Three lines and you are on your way.

grammar.title: Buying a ticket
grammar.pattern: urīd tadhkira ilā + place · bikam al-tadhkira? · matā yataḥarrak?
grammar.explain: أريد تذكرة إلى الإسكندرية من فضلك. بكم التذكرة؟ عشرون جنيهاً. متى يتحرّك القطار؟ To ask for two: تذكرتين.

examples.en: I want two tickets to Aswan.
How much is the ticket to Mansoura?
When does the next train leave?

mistakes.why: إلى marks the destination; في means inside.
بكم is already a question; من is not needed.

dialogue.t: أريد تذكرة إلى المنصورة من فضلك.
dialogue.r: urīd tadhkira ilā al-Manṣūra min faḍlik.
dialogue.en: I want a ticket to Mansoura, please.
One way or return?
One way. How much?

dialogue.t: خمسة وأربعون جنيهاً، والقطار يتحرّك السابعة والنصف.
dialogue.r: khamsa wa-arbaʿūn junayhan, wa-l-qiṭār yataḥarrak al-sābiʿa wa-l-niṣf.
dialogue.en: Forty-five pounds, and the train leaves at half past seven.

lessons.title: Where exactly? أمام، بجانب، مقابل
lessons.learn: Give a landmark and a relation, not a coordinate: أمام المسجد، بجانب الصيدلية، مقابل البنك. يقع is the verb for where something sits.

grammar.title: Landmark + relation
grammar.pattern: yaqaʿ + place + amām / bi-jānib / muqābil + landmark
grammar.explain: يقع البنك مقابل الحديقة. The relation word takes the genitive: أمام المسجد، بجانب الصيدلية. In speech the ending is dropped: البنك مقابل الحديقة.

examples.en: The pharmacy is next to the bakery.
The hotel is in front of the station.
The café is opposite the university.

mistakes.why: After بجانب the noun is genitive: المخبزِ, written plainly as المخبز.
Relation words take a direct genitive, not لـ.

dialogue.en: Where is the pharmacy, please?
Next to the bakery, in front of the mosque.
And the café?

dialogue.t: المقهى مقابل الحديقة، على بعد خطوات.
dialogue.r: al-maqhā muqābil al-ḥadīqa, ʿalā buʿd khuṭuwāt.
dialogue.en: The café is opposite the park, a few steps away.

lessons.title: Eleven to a hundred
lessons.learn: Arabic builds the teens and tens by joining: أحد عشر (11), واحد وعشرون (21), مئة (100). The units come first, the ten follows with و.

grammar.title: Units before tens
grammar.explain: خمسة وعشرون (25), ثلاثة وستون (63), تسعة وتسعون (99). The counted noun stays singular accusative after 11–99 in careful Arabic: خمسة وعشرون كتاباً.

examples.en: The price is a hundred pounds.

mistakes.why: The unit comes first in Arabic: 25 is 'five-and-twenty'.
After 11–99 the counted noun is singular accusative.

dialogue.en: How many books do you want?
I want twenty-three books.

dialogue.t: كلّ كتاب بخمسة جنيهات، إذاً مئة وخمسة عشر.
dialogue.r: kull kitāb bi-khamsat junayhāt, idhan miʾa wa-khamsata ʿashar.
dialogue.en: Each book is five pounds, so that is a hundred and fifteen.
All right — a hundred and twenty with delivery.

lessons.title: Phone numbers and addresses
lessons.learn: A phone number is read digit by digit: صفر، واحد، اثنان… An address runs building, street, district, and يقع carries the whole of it.

grammar.title: Reading a number aloud
grammar.pattern: digit + digit … · raqm + number · al-ʿunwān huwa…
grammar.explain: هاتفي هو صفر واحد اثنان… Real speech often drops the و between digits. Addresses run small to large: رقم 12، شارع النيل، الزمالك.

examples.en: My address: Nile Street, building ten.

mistakes.why: Two nouns in a row need an idafa or an adjective; رقم هاتفي is the idafa.

mistakes.wrong: أسكن في شارع النيل، والعنوان في الزمالك.
mistakes.why: The district follows the street directly; في is not repeated.

dialogue.en: What is your phone number, please?

dialogue.t: صفر واحد صفر اثنان ثلاثة أربعة خمسة ستة سبعة.
dialogue.r: ṣifr wāḥid ṣifr ithnān thalātha arbaʿa khamsa sitta sabʿa.
dialogue.en: Zero one zero two three four five six seven.
And the address?

dialogue.t: شارع النيل، مبنى عشرة، الطابق الثالث.
dialogue.r: shāriʿ al-nīl, mabnā ʿashara, al-ṭābiq al-thālith.
dialogue.en: Nile Street, building ten, third floor.

lessons.title: Prices: too expensive, can you lower it?
lessons.learn: Bargaining runs on four lines: بكم؟، غالي، هل يمكن أن تخفض؟، حسناً آخذه. Keep it friendly — غالي alone sounds like a complaint, غالي قليلاً softens it.

grammar.title: Bargaining frames
grammar.pattern: bikam? · ghālī qalīlan · hal yumkin an takhfiḍ? · ḥasanan, ākhudhuhu
grammar.explain: بكم هذه الحقيبة؟ خمسون. غالي قليلاً — هل يمكن أن تخفض؟ خمسة وأربعون. حسناً، آخذها. The object agrees: آخذها for a feminine noun, آخذه for a masculine one.

examples.en: All right, I'll take it at this price.

mistakes.why: هل يمكن أن… is the polite request frame; أريد أن + another subject sounds like a demand.
رخيص describes an object, not the price you negotiated.

dialogue.en: A little expensive — can you lower it?
Forty-five, and that is the last price.

lessons.title: The days of the week
lessons.learn: The Arabic week runs from السبت. Across the region the same names mostly hold, and Friday is the day everyone knows by name.

grammar.title: Days are adverbial
grammar.pattern: yawm + day · min + day ilā + day

lessons.title: Making a plan, refusing one kindly
lessons.learn: عندي موعد is the reason, للأسف does the softening, and المرة القادمة keeps the door open. Arabic almost never refuses without offering another time.

grammar.title: Making and refusing
grammar.pattern: hal yumkin an…? · ʿindī mawʿid · li-l-asaf, al-marra al-qādima
grammar.explain: هل يمكن أن نلتقي الجمعة؟ للأسف، عندي موعد — هل يمكن يوم الأحد؟ The whole negotiation is three moves: propose, decline with a reason, propose again.

examples.en: Unfortunately I am busy in the morning.

examples.t: إذاً، المرة القادمة إن شاء الله.
examples.r: idhan, al-marra al-qādima in shāʾa Allāh.

mistakes.right: للأسف، عندي موعد. هل يمكن يوم آخر؟
mistakes.why: A bare no closes the conversation; Arabic declines with a reason and an alternative.
Time adverbs of this type take the accusative: صباحاً.

dialogue.r: li-l-asaf, ʿindī mawʿid ṣabāḥan. hal yumkin baʿda al-ẓuhr?
dialogue.en: Unfortunately I have an appointment in the morning. Can we do the afternoon?

items.q: Say: Where is the pharmacy, please?
يفتح المتحف الساعة التاسعة صباحاً. When does it open?
«غالي قليلاً — هل يمكن أن تخفض؟» What is the speaker doing?
اركب الحافلة رقم خمسة وعشرين من المحطة. What is this about?
الاجتماع الساعة التاسعة صباحاً. When is the meeting?

culture.text: Getting around an Arab city runs on landmarks rather than street names: the pharmacy, the mosque, the bakery. A direction that names a landmark is understood by everyone, and a visitor who learns ten landmarks stops being a tourist. In many cities taxis are shared, so a driver may pick up another passenger mid-route — it is normal, not a detour.

reading.text: أريد الذهاب إلى المتحف. من فضلك، هل هو بعيد؟ اركب الحافلة رقم خمسة وعشرين، ثمّ انعطف يميناً عند الصيدلية. الأجرة عشرة جنيهات. المتحف مقابل الحديقة الكبيرة، ويفتح الساعة التاسعة صباحاً.
reading.gloss: I want to go to the museum. Please, is it far? Take bus number twenty-five, then turn right at the pharmacy. The fare is ten pounds. The museum is opposite the big park, and it opens at nine in the morning.

listening.script:
أ: بكم التذكرة إلى المنصورة؟
ب: خمسة وأربعون جنيهاً.
أ: ومتى يتحرّك القطار؟
ب: الساعة السابعة والنصف مساءً، من المحطة الثانية.
listening.gloss: A: How much is the ticket to Mansoura? B: Forty-five pounds. A: And when does the train leave? B: At half past seven in the evening, from platform two.

idioms.meaning: out of sight of the public
the final stop, the end of the line
to the right; on the right-hand side

mistakes.why: أين and يقع both ask the place; keep one.
بجانب takes a direct genitive, without من.
Ordinal hour, adverbial مساءً; no في.

task.title: Direct me across your city
task.instructions: Pick a route you take often: home to work, or to the market. Write six Arabic steps with at least three landmarks and one transport line, then read it to a partner who must draw the route without asking a question. If they get lost, the missing word was probably a relation (أمام، بجانب، مقابل) — fix it and try again.
